what: serial re-timing of the certified-checker census on a second aarch64 machine: the same 4105 sealed containers replayed through the same emitted assembly, one process at a time

corpus.source: the same sealed input containers as census.tsv (see provenance.json beside this file); replayed in the incumbent census's row order
corpus.identity: verdict identity re-established against census.tsv row-wise: family, certificate stem, exit code, and stored verdict line agree byte-for-byte on all 4105 rows; only the wall column differs

checker.name: qtslab (the certified checker; see the book's front matter for its overall standing)
checker.toolchain: gcc 13.3 -O2, aarch64 (compiled on this machine from the same emitted assembly and the audit pack's FFI basis file)
checker.theorem_note: the machine-code theorem binds the emitted assembly, which is byte-identical to the incumbent census's emission (md5 above); see provenance.json

agreement.verdict_identity: 4105/4105 rows agree with census.tsv on every column but the wall; accept 4105, diverge 0, matching the incumbent and the seal-twin lane

protocol.machine: axion (see MACHINES.md): GCP c4a-standard-16 spot, Google Axion, Arm Neoverse-V2, aarch64, 16 vCPU, 64 GiB; dedicated box, sole tenant
protocol.parallelism: fully serial: one single-threaded checker process at a time, pinned to a single core with taskset; no concurrent families
protocol.walls: single-shot per certificate, wall clock measured around the checker process alone; load average 0.00/0.02/0.08 at start of the block (sole tenant), total block wall 96.8 s
protocol.verdict_field: first stdout line truncated to 120 characters, matching the incumbent census's column convention

files.census.axion.tsv: one row per certificate: family, certificate stem, exit code, first verdict line (120-character prefix), wall-clock seconds
